proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\beta\in\mathcal K\), and put
\[
\mathcal A_{\beta}
=\mathfrak R_{\beta}(\mathfrak M)\cap\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{HD}}.
\]
The inclusion \(\mathcal A_{\beta}\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{HD}}\) follows directly from the definition of intersection.  We prove that it is proper by constructing one deterministic triangular array in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{HD}}\) that violates a member condition of \(\mathfrak M\).

Choose a unit vector \(a\in\mathbb R^{p}\) and a bounded deterministic triangular array \(\{\widetilde x_{in}:i\le n\}\) such that, along the admissible values of \(n\),
\[
\widetilde x_{1n}=0,\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\widetilde x_{in}=0,\qquad
\widetilde S_{xx,n}
=\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}
\widetilde x_{in}\widetilde x_{in}^{\mathsf T}
\longrightarrow\Sigma,
\qquad \Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}.
\]
Such an array is obtained, for example, by cycling through bounded antipodal coordinate vectors and using a bounded final incomplete cycle.  Define the contaminated baseline and the potential outcomes by
\[
x_{1n}^{\star}=n^{1/4}a,\qquad
x_{in}^{\star}=\widetilde x_{in}\quad(2\le i\le n),
\qquad
Y_{in}^{\star}(q)=a^{\mathsf T}x_{in}^{\star}
\quad(q\in\mathcal Q).
\]
Its baseline mean is \(\bar x_n^{\star}=n^{-3/4}a\).  Therefore its finite-population covariance is exactly
\[
S_{xx,n}^{\star}
=\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}
(x_{in}^{\star}-\bar x_n^{\star})
(x_{in}^{\star}-\bar x_n^{\star})^{\mathsf T}
=\widetilde S_{xx,n}
+\frac{n^{1/2}-n^{-1/2}}{n-1}aa^{\mathsf T}
\longrightarrow\Sigma.
\]
In particular, \(S_{xx,n}^{\star}\) and its limit are nonsingular for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The outcome means and all covariance quantities required by Han and Deng also converge, because
\[
\bar Y_n^{\star}(q)=a^{\mathsf T}\bar x_n^{\star}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
S_{qq,n}^{\star}=a^{\mathsf T}S_{xx,n}^{\star}a
\longrightarrow a^{\mathsf T}\Sigma a,
\qquad
S_{q,x,n}^{\star}=a^{\mathsf T}S_{xx,n}^{\star},
\]
and the unit-level nonconstant factorial effects are zero: the columns of the nonconstant Walsh matrix satisfy \(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}c_q=0\), whence
\[
2^{1-K_f}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}c_qY_{in}^{\star}(q)
=2^{1-K_f}\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}c_q\right)
a^{\mathsf T}x_{in}^{\star}=0.
\]
Thus the corresponding finite-population factorial-effect covariance converges to zero.

The maximum-negligibility conditions also hold.  Indeed,
\[
\frac{\max_{i\le n}\lVert x_{in}^{\star}-\bar x_n^{\star}\rVert^2}{n}
=O(n^{-1/2})\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\frac{\max_{i\le n,q\in\mathcal Q}
|Y_{in}^{\star}(q)-\bar Y_n^{\star}(q)|^2}{n}
=O(n^{-1/2})\longrightarrow0.
\]
If Han and Deng's split-size denominator is retained, take any balanced split with first-wave fraction bounded away from zero; the same two displays then hold with that denominator.  This does not restrict the published deterministic-array class after its allocation-share clause is removed.

It remains to verify Han and Deng's Assumption \(3\).  Let \(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{x,n}\) denote the vector obtained by stacking the \(F\) factorial contrasts of the baseline means.  Because \(Y_{in}^{\star}(q)=a^{\mathsf T}x_{in}^{\star}\) for every \(q\), the factorial outcome estimator obeys the exact identity
\[
\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{n}^{\star}
=(I_F\otimes a^{\mathsf T})\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{x,n}.
\]
Consequently the estimator is entirely in the linear span of the covariate-imbalance vector, and its projected covariance is
\[
V_{\tau\tau,n}^{\parallel,\star}
=(I_F\otimes a^{\mathsf T})
V_{xx,n}^{\star}
(I_F\otimes a).
\]
Balanced allocation and orthogonality of the nonconstant Walsh columns give a positive scalar \(\kappa_n\), converging to \(\kappa>0\), for which
\[
V_{xx,n}^{\star}=\kappa_n(I_F\otimes S_{xx,n}^{\star}),
\qquad
V_{\tau\tau,n}^{\parallel,\star}
=\kappa_n(a^{\mathsf T}S_{xx,n}^{\star}a)I_F
\longrightarrow
\kappa(a^{\mathsf T}\Sigma a)I_F\in\mathbb S_{++}^{F}.
\]
Thus both the finite projected covariance (eventually) and its limit are nonsingular.  After changing finitely many initial rows if necessary, they are nonsingular for every index.  The constructed array therefore satisfies the defining Han--Deng Assumptions \(3\) and \(4\), apart from the expressly removed allocation-share clause, and hence belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{HD}}\).

On the other hand,
\[
\sup_n\max_{i\le n}\lVert x_{in}^{\star}\rVert
\ge \sup_n n^{1/4}=\infty.
\]
This violates \(\mathrm{ass{:}baseline\text{-}bound}\), which is a member property of \(\mathfrak M\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\).  Hence the witness belongs to no \(\mathfrak R_{\beta}(\mathfrak M)\), and in particular it is not in \(\mathcal A_{\beta}\).  We have proved
\[
\mathcal A_{\beta}\subsetneq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{HD}}.
\]
The witness does not depend on \(\beta\), so the conclusion holds for every \(\beta\in\mathcal K\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(\beta\in\mathcal K\), the unconditional class relation implied by the frozen assumptions is
\[
\mathfrak R_{\beta}(\mathfrak M)\cap\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{HD}}
\subsetneq \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{HD}}.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Han and Deng's Assumption 3 requires the full \(F\)-dimensional projected factorial covariance and its limit to be nonsingular. The frozen oracle-rank condition requires only a common positive rank \(r_G\), and does not impose \(r_G=F\) or nonvanishing unnormalized projected covariance. Thus the un-intersected inclusion is stronger than the frozen premises. The replacement leaves the published class unchanged and restricts the left-hand side to a subclass of the original realization class; the proof certifies strictness with an explicit Han--Deng array excluded by the frozen baseline bound.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(w_q=2^{1-K_f}c_q\).  First fix a nonempty balanced set \(T\), a legal action \(H\), and a realized potential-outcome table.  The support floor in \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}mixture}\) gives
\[
 p_{T,H}(z)\geq \frac{\eta}{|\Omega_T|},
 \qquad
 \pi_{iq}(T,H)\geq \frac{\eta}{Q}>0.
\]
The second inequality follows because exactly \(|\Omega_T|/Q\) balanced assignments put unit \(i\) at treatment combination \(q\).  Thus every division in the Horvitz--Thompson formula is valid.  By the definition of \(\pi_{iq}(T,H)\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{p_{T,H}}\!\left[\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)\mid \mathbf Y_n,\mathbf X_n\right]
 &=\frac1{|T|}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
 w_qY_{in}(q)\frac{P_{p_{T,H}}(Z_i=q)}{\pi_{iq}(T,H)}\\
 &=\frac1{|T|}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}w_qY_{in}(q)
 =\boldsymbol\tau_T.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This calculation uses neither label symmetry nor equality of the first-order inclusion probabilities.

For a fixed split \(S=S_m\), write \(T=S^c\) and
\[
 e_S=\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_S(0)-\boldsymbol\tau_S,
 \qquad
 e_T=\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(\delta_m)-\boldsymbol\tau_T.
\]
The finite-population identity
\[
 \boldsymbol\tau_n=\frac mn\boldsymbol\tau_S+\frac Nn\boldsymbol\tau_T
\]
follows directly by partitioning the unit sum.  Conditional on \(S\), the full potential-outcome table, and the pilot sigma-field \(\mathcal O_m\), the action \(\delta_m\) is fixed and the preceding Horvitz--Thompson calculation gives \(E(e_T\mid S,\mathbf Y_n,\mathbf X_n,\mathcal O_m)=0\).  Since \(e_S\) is measurable with respect to these conditioning variables,
\[
 E(e_S^{\mathsf T}We_T\mid S,\mathbf Y_n,\mathbf X_n,\mathcal O_m)=0.
\]
Consequently, after averaging over the outcome law in \(\mathrm{ass{:}stable\text{-}product\text{-}law}\),
\[
 R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)
 =\left(\frac mn\right)^2E_{S_m}V_{S_m}(0,\beta)
 +\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta).
 \tag{1}
\]
The product law is used here only to ensure that, conditional on the split, the unobserved main-wave outcome table has its stated conditional law independently of the pilot outcomes on which \(\delta_m\) depends.  The conditional centering itself was design based and held for every fixed table.

It remains to identify the complete-randomization part of (1).  When \(H=0\), all imbalance scores tie, so the common boundary randomization has \(a_{T,0}(z)=\alpha\) for every \(z\in\Omega_T\).  Hence \(p_{T,0}\) is uniform on \(\Omega_T\) and \(\pi_{iq}(T,0)=1/Q\).  Generate a uniform \(m\)-subset, independently assign its units uniformly over its balanced support, and do the same on its complement.  For any fixed \(z\in\Omega_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}\), the number of compatible pilot subsets is
\[
 \prod_{q\in\mathcal Q}{n/Q\choose m/Q},
\]
which does not depend on \(z\).  Therefore the combined assignment is uniform on \(\Omega_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}\).  Moreover, the two weighted wave estimators combine pointwise to the full-sample Horvitz--Thompson estimator because
\[
 \frac mn\frac1m\sum_{i\in S}\sum_q\frac{w_q\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}Y_{in}(q)}{1/Q}
 +\frac Nn\frac1N\sum_{i\in T}\sum_q\frac{w_q\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}Y_{in}(q)}{1/Q}
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_q\frac{w_q\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}Y_{in}(q)}{1/Q}.
\]
Applying the already proved cross-term cancellation with both actions equal to zero yields
\[
 V_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(0,\beta)
 =\left(\frac mn\right)^2E_{S_m}V_{S_m}(0,\beta)
 +\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E_{S_m}V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(0,\beta).
 \tag{2}
\]
Subtract \(R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)=V_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(G_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta),\beta)\) from (1), substitute (2), and add and subtract \((N/n)^2E V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)\).  The definition of \(d_T\) then gives exactly
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
 &=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
 -\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)\\
 &\quad+\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E\!\left[
 V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)
 -V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)
 \right].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Randomized boundary ties affect only the numerical values of \(p_{T,H}\) and \(\pi_{iq}\), not any equality above.  Unequal inclusion probabilities are retained in every inverse-probability factor.  An ordinary symmetric estimator replaces those factors by the common value \(Q\), so it does not represent the unequal-inclusion case in general.

Let \(M_T(\beta)=\mathcal B_T(\beta)^{\mathsf T}W\mathcal B_T(\beta)\).  Since \(W\) is positive definite, \(M_T(\beta)\) is positive semidefinite.  If \(M_T(\beta)=0\), then the zero convention in \(\mathcal N\) gives \(G_T(\beta)=0\).  Otherwise a nonzero positive-semidefinite matrix has strictly positive trace, and
\[
 G_T(\beta)=\frac{M_T(\beta)}{\operatorname{tr}M_T(\beta)}
 \in\mathbb S_+^{Fp},
 \qquad \operatorname{tr}G_T(\beta)=1.
\]
Thus \(G_T(\beta)\in\mathcal H_T\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}admissible\text{-}action}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}action\text{-}space}\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}mixture}\),
\[
 |\Omega_T|^{-1}\sum_{z\in\Omega_T}a_{T,G_T(\beta)}(z)=\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_T}p_{T,G_T(\beta)}(z)
 =\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}|\Omega_T|^{-1}\sum_z a_{T,G_T(\beta)}(z)=1.
\]
Finally,
\[
 p_{T,G_T(\beta)}(z)
 =|\Omega_T|^{-1}\left\{\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}a_{T,G_T(\beta)}(z)\right\}
 \geq \frac{\eta}{|\Omega_T|}>0.
\]
These are respectively exact acceptance mass, normalization, and the asserted support floor.

Conditional on the pilot sigma-field \(\mathcal O_m\), the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{eff}}\) evaluates the empirical oracle construction on the main-wave set and applies the normalization \(\mathcal N\).  The unnormalized matrix has the form \(\mathcal B^{\mathsf T}W\mathcal B\), hence is positive semidefinite; normalization sends it either to zero or to a positive-semidefinite matrix of trace one.  Therefore, almost surely,
\[
 \widehat G_m=0
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad
 \widehat G_m\in\mathbb S_+^{Fp},\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\widehat G_m)=1.
\]
Thus \(\widehat G_m\in\mathcal H_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}action\text{-}space}\).  Conditional on the pilot realization, \(\widehat G_m\) is fixed, so \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}mixture}\) gives
\[
 |\Omega_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}|^{-1}
 \sum_z a_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}},\widehat G_m}(z)=\alpha
\]
and
\[
 p_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}},\widehat G_m}(z)
 \geq \frac{\eta}{|\Omega_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}|}>0.
\]
Because these conclusions hold for every pilot realization, they hold almost surely without any symmetry condition on the learned score.

Fix the potential-outcome table and let \(U_T\) denote the uniform law on \(\Omega_T\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}mixture}\),
\[
 \frac{p_{T,H}(z)}{U_T(z)}
 =\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}a_{T,H}(z)\leq L,
 \qquad
 \pi_{iq}(T,H)\geq\frac{\eta}{Q}.
 \tag{3}
\]
For a scalar coordinate after applying \(W^{1/2}\), write the estimator as
\[
 k^{-1}\sum_{i\in T}f_i(Z_i),
 \qquad
 f_i(q)=\frac{e^{\mathsf T}W^{1/2}w_qY_{in}(q)}{\pi_{iq}(T,H)},
\]
where \(e\) is a Euclidean coordinate vector.  Under balanced complete randomization, direct enumeration of the two labels assigned to distinct units gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{U_T}\{f_i(Z_i),f_j(Z_j)\}
 =-\frac{1}{k-1}\operatorname{Cov}_{q\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal Q)}\{f_i(q),f_j(q)\},
 \qquad i\ne j.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_{U_T}\!\left\{\sum_{i\in T}f_i(Z_i)\right\}
 &=\frac{k}{k-1}\sum_{i\in T}\operatorname{Var}_{q}\{f_i(q)\}
 -\frac{1}{k-1}\operatorname{Var}_{q}\!\left\{\sum_{i\in T}f_i(q)\right\}\\
 &\leq \frac{k}{k-1}\sum_{i\in T}E_q f_i(q)^2.
 \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(c=E_{U_T}[k^{-1}\sum_i f_i(Z_i)]\).  Exact Horvitz--Thompson unbiasedness under \(p_{T,H}\), proved in \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}ht\text{-}accounting}\), and the likelihood-ratio bound (3) imply
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{p_{T,H}}\!\left\{k^{-1}\sum_i f_i(Z_i)\right\}
 \leq E_{p_{T,H}}\!\left[\left\{k^{-1}\sum_i f_i(Z_i)-c\right\}^2\right]
 \leq L\operatorname{Var}_{U_T}\!\left\{k^{-1}\sum_i f_i(Z_i)\right\}.
\]
Sum this inequality over an orthonormal coordinate basis and use (3)--(4).  Since \(k\geq Q=2^{K_f}\geq4\), one has \(k/(k-1)\leq4/3\).  Therefore, conditional on the table,
\[
 E_{p_{T,H}}\!\left[
 (\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)-\boldsymbol\tau_T)^{\mathsf T}
 W(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)-\boldsymbol\tau_T)
 \right]
 \leq \frac{4LQ}{3\eta^2k^2}
 \left\{\max_q w_q^{\mathsf T}Ww_q\right\}
 \sum_{i\in T}\sum_qY_{in}(q)^2.
\]
Averaging over \(P_{\beta,n}(d\mathbf Y_n\mid\mathbf X_n)\) proves the displayed claim.  In particular a common bound on the average conditional second moment makes the right-hand side a common constant times \(k^{-1}\).

The original supremum over all members of \(\mathfrak M\) cannot be recovered from \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\): that assumption supplies only a memberwise finite bound and fixes no common numerical envelope.  More concretely, start from any admissible bounded regular conditional family and apply the one-to-one rescaling \(Y(q)\mapsto M Y(q)\).  For each finite \(M\) the memberwise boundedness, quadratic-mean differentiability, and Fisher information are preserved under this pushforward; the trace-normalized oracle action is unchanged, while every quadratic design risk is multiplied by \(M^2\).  Letting \(M\) range over finite constants is an explicit generic-class certificate that the unqualified model-class supremum is infinite.

Set \(d=Fp\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}experiment\text{-}indexed\text{-}oracle\text{-}convergence}\), every \(G_{\infty}(\beta)\) is a limit of nonzero trace-normalized oracle scores.  Hence it is positive semidefinite with trace one.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}oracle\text{-}rank}\), its rank is the fixed positive integer \(r_G\).  The max--min variational formulas for ordered eigenvalues show directly that they are continuous functions of a symmetric matrix in operator norm.  Continuity on compact \(\mathcal K\) and the constant-rank condition therefore give a number \(\lambda_->0\) such that every positive eigenvalue of every \(G_{\infty}(\beta)\) belongs to \([\lambda_-,1]\).

Rotational invariance of \(Z\) shows that
\[
 Z^{\mathsf T}G_{\infty}(\beta)Z
 \ \stackrel{d}{=}\ \sum_{j=1}^{r_G}\lambda_j(\beta)\xi_j^2,
\]
where the \(\xi_j\) are independent standard normal variables and the ordered positive eigenvalues \(\lambda_j(\beta)\) are continuous as an unordered multiset.  Convolution of the scaled chi-square densities shows that the right-hand side has a finite, continuous, strictly positive density at every \(u>0\).  The same convolution formula, dominated on compact subsets of \((0,\infty)\) by the bounds \(\lambda_j\in[\lambda_-,1]\), makes its distribution function and density jointly continuous in \((\beta,u)\).

The inequalities
\[
 \lambda_-\chi^2_{r_G}\leq\sum_{j=1}^{r_G}\lambda_j(\beta)\xi_j^2\leq\chi^2_{r_G}
\]
hold under the displayed coupling.  Since \(0<\alpha<1\), they place all \(q_{\alpha,\beta}\) in one compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\).  Joint continuity and strict monotonicity of the distribution functions then imply continuity of \(\beta\mapsto q_{\alpha,\beta}\).  Joint continuity and positivity of the density on the compact quantile graph give
\[
 0<\min_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_\beta(q_{\alpha,\beta})
 \leq\max_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_\beta(q_{\alpha,\beta})<\infty.
\]

For completeness, continuity of the coarea moments can be checked without selecting eigenvectors globally.  The spectral projection onto the range of \(G_{\infty}(\beta)\) is continuous because the spectrum is uniformly separated from zero.  On a neighborhood of any fixed \(\beta\), projecting a fixed basis and applying Gram--Schmidt supplies continuous orthonormal frames for the range and null space.  In these coordinates the positive range block \(A_\beta\) has eigenvalues in \([\lambda_-,1]\).  On the level set \(r^{\mathsf T}A_\beta r=u\), make the change of variables
\[
 r=\sqrt u\,A_\beta^{-1/2}\omega,
 \qquad \omega\in\mathbb S^{r_G-1}.
\]
After the null Gaussian coordinates are integrated out, each denominator, first moment, and second moment in the definition of \(\mathcal C\) is an integral over the fixed unit sphere of a polynomial in \(\omega\), \(D_{\rho_a}G_{\infty}(\beta)\), and \(D_{\rho_b}G_{\infty}(\beta)\), multiplied by a Gaussian factor and continuous determinant powers of \(A_\beta\).  On a compact neighborhood of the quantile graph these integrands have one common integrable bound because \(u\) is bounded away from zero and the eigenvalues are in \([\lambda_-,1]\).  Dominated convergence therefore gives continuity of all raw coarea moments.  The denominator equals the strictly positive density just treated, so taking ratios and subtracting products proves continuity of \(\mathcal C(\beta,u)\).

The defining formula for \(\Gamma\), together with continuity of \(f\), \(q\), and \(\mathcal C\), proves continuity of \(\Gamma\).  Finally, under the additional condition stated in the narrowed claim, inversion is continuous on \(\mathbb S_{++}^r\); compactness keeps the inverse bounded.  Composition with matrix multiplication and trace then proves continuity of \(B\).  The frozen dependencies do not impose continuity of \(I_{\mathrm{eff}}\), which is why the last conclusion is necessarily conditional.

Fix a unit \(i\).  Treatment-label flips act transitively on \(\mathcal Q\).  Invariance of \(p_{T,H}\) therefore implies that \(P(Z_i=q)\) has the same value for every \(q\).  These \(Q\) probabilities sum to one, so
\[
 \pi_{iq}(T,H)=\frac1Q.
\]
Substitution into the Horvitz--Thompson formula gives
\[
 \widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}w_q
 \left\{\frac{Q}{|T|}\sum_{i\in T:Z_i=q}Y_{in}(q)\right\},
\]
which is exactly the balanced factorial contrast of the treatment-cell means.

When \(H=0\), every assignment score is zero.  Common randomized boundary treatment and exact mass \(\alpha\) force \(a_{T,0}(z)=\alpha\) for every balanced assignment, hence \(p_{T,0}\) is uniform.  For any full balanced assignment \(z\), the number of pilot subsets that contain exactly \(m/Q\) units from each of its treatment cells is
\[
 \prod_{q\in\mathcal Q}{n/Q\choose m/Q},
\]
independent of \(z\).  The split followed by independent balanced randomization in its two waves thus induces the uniform law on the full balanced support.  The pointwise pooling calculation in \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}ht\text{-}accounting}\) shows that the pooled estimator equals the full-sample estimator.  These are exact finite-design assertions.  The removed asymptotic sentence would require additional triangular-array hypotheses that are absent from the frozen dependency list.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \((\mathsf X,\mathscr A,\mathsf P)\) be a probability space, let \(L\) be integrable, and let \(0<\alpha<1\).  Suppose \(a_0,a:\mathsf X\to[0,1]\) satisfy \(E_{\mathsf P}a_0=E_{\mathsf P}a=\alpha\), and for some \(q\in\mathbb R\), \(a_0=1\) on \(\{L<q\}\) and \(a_0=0\) on \(\{L>q\}\).  Then
\[
 E_{\mathsf P}\{(L-q)(a-a_0)\}\geq0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \inf_{\substack{0\leq b\leq1\\E_{\mathsf P}b=\alpha}}E_{\mathsf P}(Lb)
 =\sup_{v\in\mathbb R}\left[\alpha v-E_{\mathsf P}\{(v-L)_+\}\right],
\]
and every lower-tail rule with common randomization on its boundary attains the infimum.  These statements remain exact when \(\mathsf P\) has atoms.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
On \(\{L<q\}\), one has \(L-q<0\) and \(a-a_0=a-1\leq0\); on \(\{L>q\}\), one has \(L-q>0\) and \(a-a_0=a\geq0\); and on \(\{L=q\}\) the product is zero.  Thus \((L-q)(a-a_0)\geq0\) pointwise, proving the first assertion after integration.

For any feasible \(b\) and any \(v\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 E(Lb)=\alpha v+E\{(L-v)b\}
 \geq \alpha v-E\{(v-L)_+\},
\]
because \((L-v)b\geq L-v\) on \(\{L<v\}\) and \((L-v)b\geq0\) on \(\{L\geq v\}\).  Taking the supremum over \(v\) gives the lower bound.  Choose a quantile \(q\) and randomize with one common probability on \(\{L=q\}\) so that the mass is exactly \(\alpha\).  For the resulting lower-tail rule \(a_0\), both pointwise inequalities at \(v=q\) are equalities.  Hence the primal and dual values coincide and \(a_0\) attains them.  No continuity of the law was used.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal K\) is compact and \(A,B:\mathcal K\to(0,\infty)\) are continuous.  For \(\Phi(t)=\max_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\{A(\beta)t+B(\beta)/t\}\), there is a unique minimizer \(t^{\star}>0\), and
\[
 \Phi(t^{\star})
 =\max_{(a,b)\in\operatorname{conv}\{(A(\beta),B(\beta)):\beta\in\mathcal K\}}2\sqrt{ab}.
\]
There are at most two parameter values active at \(t^{\star}\) and weights on them whose coefficient average \((a^{\star},b^{\star})\) attains the last maximum, with \(t^{\star}=\sqrt{b^{\star}/a^{\star}}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Continuity and compactness give constants \(0<a_-\leq A\leq a_+<\infty\) and \(0<b_-\leq B\leq b_+<\infty\).  Put \(t=e^s\).  Every function
\[
 f_\beta(s)=A(\beta)e^s+B(\beta)e^{-s}
\]
satisfies
\[
 f_\beta''(s)=f_\beta(s)\geq2\sqrt{a_-b_-}.
\]
Subtracting \(\sqrt{a_-b_-}\,s^2\) shows directly that all \(f_\beta\) have a common positive strong-convexity modulus; taking their pointwise maximum preserves convexity after this subtraction.  Hence \(s\mapsto\Phi(e^s)\) is strongly convex.  It is coercive because it is bounded below by \(a_-e^s+b_-e^{-s}\).  It therefore has exactly one minimizer \(s^{\star}\), and \(t^{\star}=e^{s^{\star}}\) is the unique minimizer in the original coordinate.

Let \(\mathcal A^{\star}=\{\beta:A(\beta)t^{\star}+B(\beta)/t^{\star}=\Phi(t^{\star})\}\).  Compactness makes this active set nonempty.  The left and right derivatives of a maximum of differentiable scalar functions show that zero lies in
\[
 \operatorname{conv}\left\{A(\beta)-\frac{B(\beta)}{(t^{\star})^2}:\beta\in\mathcal A^{\star}\right\}.
\]
Because this is a convex hull in one dimension, either one active derivative is zero or two active derivatives bracket zero.  Thus there are at most two active points \(\beta_j\) and weights \(\lambda_j\) such that
\[
 a^{\star}=\sum_j\lambda_jA(\beta_j),\qquad
 b^{\star}=\sum_j\lambda_jB(\beta_j),\qquad
 a^{\star}=\frac{b^{\star}}{(t^{\star})^2}.
\]
Every selected point is active, so
\[
 \Phi(t^{\star})=a^{\star}t^{\star}+\frac{b^{\star}}{t^{\star}}
 =2\sqrt{a^{\star}b^{\star}}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Conversely, for every \((a,b)\) in the displayed convex hull and every \(t>0\), linearity in \((a,b)\) gives
\[
 at+\frac bt\leq\Phi(t).
\]
At \(t=t^{\star}\), the arithmetic--geometric mean inequality yields \(2\sqrt{ab}\leq at^{\star}+b/t^{\star}\leq\Phi(t^{\star})\).  Maximizing over the convex hull and combining with (5) proves the equality and the two-point certificate.

Let \(k=|T|\), \(w_q=2^{1-K_f}c_q\), and \(L=\eta+(1-\eta)/\alpha\).  For every \((\mathbf X_n,P_{\beta,n})\in\mathfrak M\), every \(\beta\in\mathcal K\), every balanced \(T\) with \(k\geq Q\), and every \(H\in\mathcal H_T\),
\[
 V_T(H,\beta)
 \leq \frac{4LQ}{3\eta^2k^2}
 \left\{\max_{q\in\mathcal Q}w_q^{\mathsf T}Ww_q\right\}
 \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}E_\beta\{Y_{in}(q)^2\mid x_{in}\}.
\]
Consequently, the asserted uniform \(O(k^{-1})\) conclusion holds on every subclass for which the displayed average second-moment envelope is bounded uniformly over its members, parameters, and balanced subsets.  No supremum over all of \(\mathfrak M\) is asserted without such a common numerical envelope.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen class requires only a memberwise finite outcome bound and fixes no common numerical envelope. Rescaling any admissible outcome family by an arbitrary finite constant preserves the qualitative model conditions and trace-normalized oracle action but multiplies design risks by the square of that constant, so the supremum over all model members is infinite. The replacement gives the exact computable inequality supported by the design.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For the common limit \(G_{\infty}\), the map \(\beta\mapsto q_{\alpha,\beta}\) is continuous, \(0<q_{\alpha,\beta}<\infty\), and
\[
0<\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_{\beta}(q_{\alpha,\beta})
\leq\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_{\beta}(q_{\alpha,\beta})<\infty.
\]
The coarea version \(\mathcal C(\beta,u)\) is continuous on a neighborhood of \(\{(\beta,q_{\alpha,\beta}):\beta\in\mathcal K\}\), and consequently \(\Gamma(\beta)\) is continuous on \(\mathcal K\).  If, in addition, \(I_{\mathrm{eff}}:\mathcal K\to\mathbb S_{++}^r\) is continuous, then \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\) is continuous on \(\mathcal K\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Constant rank and oracle smoothness prove the quantile, density, coarea, and curvature conclusions, but the frozen dependencies impose no continuity condition on the efficient-information map. Therefore unconditional continuity of the final trace functional is stronger than the premises; the corrected claim makes precisely that last implication conditional.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: If \(p_{T,H}\) is invariant under the treatment-label flip group, then \(\pi_{iq}(T,H)=1/Q\) for all \(i\in T\) and \(q\in\mathcal Q\), so \(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)\) equals the ordinary balanced factorial difference-in-means estimator.  With \(H=0\) in both waves, the pooled assignment is exactly uniform on the full-sample balanced support and the pooled estimator is pointwise the full-sample balanced complete-randomization estimator.  No asymptotic limit law is asserted without separate finite-population central-limit and covariance-limit hypotheses.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The exact symmetry and pooled-law reductions are finite combinatorial consequences of the frozen design. The original first-order limit sentence has no triangular-array Lindeberg, limiting covariance, or cited limit-theorem node among its dependencies, so it is not a theorem under the stated premises and is removed rather than assumed.

proposed_assumptions.condition: There exists a compact set \(\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^p\) containing \(\operatorname{supp}\nu\) and every \(x_{in}\) such that, for each \(q\in\mathcal Q\), the conditional first and second moments and all of their \(\rho\)-derivatives through order three are continuous and uniformly bounded on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal K\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: Weak convergence of the baseline empirical measures controls empirical conditional moments only when those moment functions are continuous and bounded on a common compact set containing the actual triangular array. The frozen smoothness condition is restricted to the support of the limiting measure and does not control off-support array points approaching that support.

proposed.justification: Positive assignment support makes every permitted one-wave Horvitz--Thompson risk uniformly first order even on irregular subsets.
proposed.gap: General Horvitz--Thompson consistency does not provide a constant uniform over the present pilot-indexed rerandomization actions.
proposed.consumer: It rules out apparent gains from assigning only a vanishing main wave and controls rare singular pilot complements.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim names outcome moments and uses exact Horvitz--Thompson centering, so its free-symbol list and proof dependency must be updated atomically.

proposed.statement: Can the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{fin}}\) establish, uniformly over \(\mathfrak M\), exact ties, arbitrary balanced deterministic baseline lattices, local action displacements of order \(m^{-1/2}\), and unequal inclusion probabilities, that the finite Horvitz--Thompson action regret on \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\) differs from the continuous-coarea Gaussian boundary quadratic form of \(G_{\infty}\) by \(o(m^{-1})\) in probability over the split, and that the contrast between \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}\) and \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\) has no additional lattice or inclusion correction at order \(m/n^2+1/(nm)\)?
proposed.justification: This is the proof boundary on which the advertised second-order constant is valid or must acquire a finite-randomization correction.
proposed.gap: Li and Ding provide a first-order random-partition central limit theorem, and Wang and Li provide quantitative Gaussian control for best-choice rerandomization; neither controls score-weighted moving-boundary moments at this scale.
proposed.consumer: A positive answer validates smooth pilot rules on integer-valued manufacturing baselines; a negative answer identifies the correction planners must include.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The new exact lower-tail lemma is a load-bearing partial result for the still-open comparison and must be wired into that question.

proposed.statement:
The quantity \(\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)\) is positive for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Let \(m=m(n)\in\mathcal M_n\) satisfy the explicit asymptotic-minimax condition
\[
\frac{\mathcal E_n(m)}{\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)}\to1.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{m}{\sqrt n}\to t^{\star},\qquad n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)\to C^{\star}=\min_{t>0}\max_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\{A(\beta)t+B(\beta)/t\}.
\]
Here \(A\) is the full-array versus random-complement deletion coefficient and \(B\) is the continuous-coarea curvature coefficient induced by the common limit \(G_{\infty}\).  The minimizer \(t^{\star}\) is unique, and
\[
C^{\star}=\max_{(a,b)\in\operatorname{conv}\{(A(\beta),B(\beta)):\beta\in\mathcal K\}}2\sqrt{ab}.
\]
An optimizer of the last display has a certificate supported on at most two parameter values active at \(t^{\star}\).
proposed.justification: The theorem turns the pointwise expansion into a unique globally defensible pilot rule with a finite certificate.
proposed.gap: Yamin's binary-arm global boundary analysis gives an approximately optimal pilot plan of order n to the two-thirds, whereas this locally rich factorial geometry requires a sharp square-root constant and a different empirical oracle.
proposed.consumer: Stable-batch replications of Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella's sequential factorial workflow can preregister the learning-wave size from a two-state worst-case certificate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proved deterministic envelope lemma supplies the uniqueness, convex-hull identity, and two-active-state portion of the theorem and must be declared in its proof spine.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Uniform convergence of the empirical oracle and its first three quotient derivatives along both the full array and every vanishing random complement.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen conditional-moment smoothness is imposed only on the support of the limiting baseline measure. It does not control moment values at actual off-support triangular-array points, so weak empirical convergence alone cannot justify passage of empirical moments to their limits.
open_obligations.attempted: Expanded the oracle into empirical conditional first and second moments, then tried weak-convergence and deletion bounds. The weak-convergence step fails at off-support array points; a common-compact continuity condition is proposed.
open_obligations.partial_result: Under the proposed common-compact moment condition, weak convergence of the empirical baseline measures implies uniform convergence of every bounded continuous empirical moment entering \(\mathcal B_T\), together with its first three \(\rho\)-derivatives.  Deleting \(m=o(n)\) bounded summands changes each such moment by \(O(m/n)\), uniformly in the realized split.  The remaining step is to propagate these convergences through the covariance pseudoinverse and trace normalization on the stated constant-rank stratum.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform second-order one-wave oracle-gain or deletion-stability expansion strong enough to leave no term at the pilot-frontier scale.
open_obligations.obstruction: First-order finite-population Gaussian convergence gives only a little-oh remainder relative to one over the wave size. At the square-root pilot scale the theorem needs cancellation or a refined order-two expansion, including exact boundary ties and unequal Horvitz--Thompson inclusions; no frozen node supplies it.
open_obligations.attempted: Centered at the empirical oracle and Taylor-expanded the random-complement empirical moments. This closes the subset algebra conditional on an order-two one-wave expansion, but that finite-randomization expansion remains unproved.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The exact accounting theorem reduces this node to a one-wave expansion.  If one establishes, uniformly on regular subsets,
\[
d_T(\beta)=\frac{A(\beta,M_T)}{|T|}+O(|T|^{-2}),
\]
where \(M_T\) is the finite vector of empirical moments and \(A(\beta,\cdot)\) has two bounded derivatives, then uniform-subset identities give \(E(M_T-M_n)=0\) and \(E\|M_T-M_n\|^2=O\{m/(nN)\}\).  Taylor expansion then yields
\[
d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}-\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}
=A(\beta,M_n)\frac{m}{n^2}+O\!\left(\frac{m}{n^3}+\frac1{n^2}\right),
\]
which has the required remainder on the interior pilot scale.  The missing part is the uniform finite-randomization expansion for \(d_T\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: The uniform local asymptotic minimax transfer from the adaptive pilot experiment to exact finite Horvitz--Thompson action loss for arbitrary measurable actions.
open_obligations.obstruction: Quadratic-mean differentiability and information regularity identify the candidate Gaussian shift, but they do not by themselves establish a uniformly efficient pilot estimator with quadratic-loss uniform integrability, localization of unrestricted actions, or the shrinking finite-boundary comparison.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the outcome-only likelihood architecture and the Gaussian boundary Hessian. The remaining bridge is precisely the finite comparison plus uniform decision-theoretic localization, so assuming the trace constant would assume the theorem's crux.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The fixed-baseline and product-law assumptions imply that the pilot likelihood ratio contains only the \(m\) revealed conditional outcome likelihood ratios.  Under the stated quadratic-mean differentiability conditions its formal central sequence is
\[
\Delta_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in S_m}s_{Z_i,\beta}(Y_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in}),
\]
with nuisance-efficient information \(I_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  The proved Gaussian boundary calculation makes the candidate quadratic action loss equal to \(h^{\mathsf T}\Gamma(\beta)h\), so an efficient Gaussian shift would give \(\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma I_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-1}\}\).  What is not established is the uniform triangular-array LAN-to-decision transfer together with the exact finite Horvitz--Thompson boundary comparison for unrestricted measurable actions.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Whether score-weighted moving-boundary moments and exact unequal-inclusion covariance admit the required uniform little-oh comparison on arbitrary bounded deterministic baseline lattices.
open_obligations.obstruction: The proved atom-safe lower-tail identity is exact at a fixed law but gives no quantitative comparison between a shrinking finite assignment boundary and its Gaussian limit. Ordinary Berry--Esseen control of unweighted probabilities is not the weighted second-order estimate requested here.
open_obligations.attempted: Used the exact lower-tail primal-dual identity to neutralize fixed-law ties and decomposed the Horvitz--Thompson correction around uniform marginals. The latter would be order two under a uniform leave-one-unit inclusion bound of order one over the wave size, but that bound is not derivable from the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved lower-tail identity shows that randomized ties and atoms do not themselves create a sign correction: at any fixed finite law the exact lower-tail rule minimizes the trimmed linear score.  For a local displacement of size \(m^{-1/2}\), it remains necessary to compare score-weighted symmetric differences of two moving quadratic sublevel sets and the exact unequal-inclusion Horvitz--Thompson covariance with their Gaussian counterparts at error \(o(m^{-1})\).  The frozen boundedness and weak empirical convergence assumptions supply no stated quantitative theorem of this strength.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The uniform second-order expansion and its matching arbitrary-action lower bound.
open_obligations.obstruction: Exact accounting isolates exactly two terms, but both coefficient-level asymptotics are unresolved: the oracle deletion term and the exact finite learned-action regret. Treating either as a hypothesis would violate the anti-laundering requirement.
open_obligations.attempted: Proved the exact decomposition and inserted the proposed coefficient expansions algebraically. This confirms there is no additional cross-wave term, while showing that the desired theorem is equivalent to the two unresolved uniform comparisons.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The exact accounting theorem proves the algebraic reduction
\[
R_{n,m}-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}
=\left\{d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}-\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}\right\}
+\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E\{V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\widehat G_m)-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}})\}.
\]
Thus the advertised expansion follows immediately once the first bracket is shown to equal \(A(\beta)m/n^2+o\{m/n^2+(nm)^{-1}\}\) uniformly and the second to equal \(B(\beta)/(nm)+o\{m/n^2+(nm)^{-1}\}\) uniformly.  Those are precisely the two unresolved finite comparison statements; the exact identity introduces no third term.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Uniform minimax lower bounds for bounded pilots, positive pilot fractions, and nonvanishing main-wave fractions outside the interior expansion.
open_obligations.obstruction: The corrected one-wave inequality is memberwise unless a common moment envelope is added, and the frozen results contain no first-order comparison showing that arbitrary finite actions cannot beat the raw Gaussian oracle over those endpoint windows.
open_obligations.attempted: Established the nearly-all-pilot argument conditional on a fixed-member moment envelope and positive full-oracle gain. The other windows require a two-point testing or first-order localization argument not present in the frozen core.
open_obligations.partial_result: For a fixed model member with a common conditional second-moment envelope, the corrected one-wave bound implies that the greatest possible contribution of a main wave of size \(N\) to the pooled risk is \(O(N/n^2)\).  Therefore, if the first-order full-oracle gain satisfies \(n d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta_0)\to A(\beta_0)>0\), every sequence with \(N=o(n)\) has excess at least \(A(\beta_0)/(2n)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and its \(n^{3/2}\)-scaled excess diverges.  Bounded-pilot and positive-fraction windows still require a first-order arbitrary-action lower comparison that is not supplied by the frozen assumptions.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The statistical transfer from the interior risk expansion and endpoint exclusions to the global minimax pilot sequence.
open_obligations.obstruction: The deterministic optimization is proved, but its premises are the still-open uniform second-order risk theorem and endpoint lemma. Therefore positivity of the finite minimax denominator and convergence of every near-minimizing pilot sequence cannot yet be concluded.
open_obligations.attempted: Proved uniqueness, the convex-hull formula, and the two-active-state certificate, and checked the subsequence argument conditional on coercive endpoint exclusion. No unconditional route bypasses the missing statistical comparisons.
open_obligations.partial_result: The deterministic part is completely settled by \(\mathrm{lem{:}deterministic\text{-}envelope\text{-}certificate}\): for continuous positive \(A,B\), the envelope has a unique minimizer and the convex-hull value has a certificate supported on at most two active parameter values.  Conditional on the uniform interior risk expansion and endpoint exclusion, balanced rounding changes \(m/\sqrt n\) by \(O(n^{-1/2})\); coercivity makes every asymptotically minimax pilot ratio precompact, and continuity plus uniqueness forces every subsequential limit to equal \(t^{\star}\).  The statistical premises of that conditional transfer remain open.
